outcomes.question: What are the six pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
outcomes.answer: The AWS Well-Architected Framework is based on six pillars: operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, and sustainability. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 13]
outcomes.modelOutput: {"status":"ANSWERED","claims":[{"text":"The AWS Well-Architected Framework is based on six pillars: operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, and sustainability.","ref":"r1c2","quote":"When architecting technology solutions, if you neglect the six pillars of operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, and sustainability, it can become challenging to build a system that delivers on your expectations and requirements."}]}

outcomes.question: Why does the framework advise to stop guessing capacity needs?
outcomes.answer:
A poor capacity decision can result in paying for expensive idle resources or suffering the performance consequences of limited capacity. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 11]
In cloud computing, users can use exactly as much capacity as needed and scale automatically in and out. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 11]
Resource saturation, which occurs when demands placed on a workload exceed its capacity, is a common reason for workload failure on premises. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 13]
Cloud environments allow monitoring of demand and workload utilization, as well as automated adjustment of resources to avoid over-provisioning or under-provisioning. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 13]

outcomes.question: What is the difference between one-way door and two-way door decisions?
outcomes.answer:
Two-way door decisions are reversible and can utilize a lightweight process. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 69]
One-way door decisions are difficult or impossible to reverse and require greater inspection prior to being made. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 69]
Organizations should centralize one-way door decisions that could be irreversible. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 26]
Two-way door decisions can be permitted to be made by lower level organizational leaders. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 26]

outcomes.question: What is the AWS Well-Architected Tool?
outcomes.answer:
The AWS Well-Architected Tool is a service in the cloud that provides a consistent process for reviewing and measuring architectures using the AWS Well-Architected Framework. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 7]
The service is provided by AWS for reviewing workloads at no charge. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 7]
The AWS Well-Architected Tool delivers recommendations to make workloads more reliable, secure, efficient, and cost-effective. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 7]
The tool helps users review their approach before development, the state of workloads before production, and the state of workloads in production. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 12]
It allows users to compare workloads to current AWS architectural best practices, monitor overall status, and gain insight into potential risks. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 12]

outcomes.question: What does recovery time objective (RTO) mean?
outcomes.answer:
Recovery Time Objective (RTO) represents the maximum acceptable delay between a service interruption and the restoration of that service. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 680]
RTO determines what an organization defines as an acceptable time window during which a service remains unavailable. [disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws.pdf, p. 13]
Unlike Mean Time to Recovery (MTTR), which represents a mean value across multiple events over time, RTO is a target or maximum allowed value for a single event that impacts availability. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 19]

outcomes.question: How should a client retry failed requests without overloading a service?
outcomes.answer:
Exponential backoff should be used to retry requests after progressively longer intervals. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 545]
Jitter should be introduced to randomize retry intervals. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 545]
Jitter prevents retries from aligning into request spikes, while exponential backoff reduces load escalation. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 545]
A maximum number of retries or elapsed time should be configured to prevent metastable failures caused by backlogs. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 545]
Retries should only be implemented at one level of the application stack to prevent compounding attempts in a retry storm. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 545]

outcomes.question: Why should a workload be aware of service quotas and constraints?
outcomes.answer:
Being aware of service quotas and resource constraints allows customers to prevent service degradation or disruption in their AWS accounts. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 470]
Proactively monitoring and automatically managing service quotas and resource constraints can help reduce failures. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 470]
If a constraint is reached unexpectedly, an account's applications or services can suffer degradation or disruption. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 24]

outcomes.question: How does the reliability pillar suggest recovering automatically from failures?
outcomes.answer:
When a failure is detected, automated capabilities should be used to take actions to remediate. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 197]
Degradations can heal automatically through internal service mechanisms or by restarting or removing resources using remediation actions. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 197]
In cloud environments, an entire resource such as a compute instance or serverless function can and generally should be replaced when restarting. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 197]
A retry strategy using limited retries with exponential backoff and jitter can be used to handle both network timeouts and dependency failures. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 197]

outcomes.question: Who is responsible for what in the shared responsibility model for security?
outcomes.answer:
Security and compliance is a shared responsibility between AWS and the customer. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
AWS is responsible for protecting the infrastructure—including hardware, software, networking, and facilities—that runs all services offered in the AWS Cloud. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
AWS manages, operates, and controls components from the host operating system and virtualization layer down to the physical security of the service facilities. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Customer responsibility is determined by the specific AWS Cloud services selected. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
The customer assumes responsibility for the guest operating system, including updates and security patches, associated application software, and configuration of the AWS provided security group firewall. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Under the model, customers are responsible for securing their applications, data, and the services they use. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 130]

outcomes.question: How should secrets and credentials be managed and rotated?
outcomes.answer:
The recommended approach to secrets management is to adhere to the guidance of remove, replace, and rotate. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 49]
Credentials that are no longer necessary for workload functioning should be safely removed. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 49]
Whenever possible, long-term credentials should be replaced with temporary or short-term credentials, such as using IAM roles instead of hard-coding an AWS secret access key. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 49]
Long-lived secrets that cannot be removed or replaced can be centrally stored, managed, and rotated on a regular basis in a service like AWS Secrets Manager. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 300]
Application and database credentials, OAuth tokens, and API tokens and keys can be stored in AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation established. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 301]

outcomes.question: What is the principle of least privilege?
outcomes.answer:
The principle of least privilege states that identities should only be allowed to perform the smallest set of actions required to carry out a specific task. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 319]
This principle balances usability, efficiency, and security. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 319]
Operating under the principle of least privilege helps limit unintended access and assists in tracking who has access to specific resources. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 319]

outcomes.answer: Secure key management encompasses the storage, rotation, access control, and monitoring of key material needed to protect data at rest for a workload. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 399]

outcomes.question: How does the operational excellence pillar recommend making changes to workloads?
outcomes.answer:
The operational excellence pillar recommends making frequent, small, and reversible changes to workloads. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Using automated deployment techniques alongside smaller, incremental changes lowers the blast radius and enables faster reversal if failures occur. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Emphasizing frequent, small, and reversible changes limits the scope of change, enabling quicker troubleshooting, remediation, and the ability to roll back. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 82]

outcomes.question: What are runbooks used for?
outcomes.answer:
Runbooks are documented processes used to achieve a specific outcome. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 141]
In cloud operations, runbooks are used to reduce risk and achieve desired outcomes. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 141]
Runbooks are often used for routine activities. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 592]
Runbooks are also useful for running game days or fulfilling rigorous reporting and auditing requirements. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 592]
Documenting procedures in runbooks is used to provide consistent and prompt responses to well-understood events. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 592]

outcomes.question: How can feature flags and A/B testing be used to experiment safely?
outcomes.answer:
Feature flags and A/B testing can be used to safely conduct experiments and gather user feedback. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 128]
AWS AppConfig Feature Flags provides the capability to create feature flags. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 128]
A/B testing is utilized for new features to validate them with real user feedback. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 128]
Feature-flag testing allows an individual feature of a new version to be flagged on and off from outside the application so each new feature can be validated one at a time. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 133]
A/B testing shows results comparing the current version across two user testing groups. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 133]

outcomes.question: What does democratize advanced technologies mean in the performance efficiency pillar?
outcomes.answer:
Democratizing advanced technologies means making advanced technology implementation easier for your team by delegating complex tasks to your cloud vendor. [wellarchitected-performance-efficiency-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Instead of having an IT team learn to host and run a new technology, organizations can consume the technology as a service. [wellarchitected-performance-efficiency-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Technologies requiring specialized expertise, like NoSQL databases, media transcoding, and machine learning, become cloud services that teams can consume. [wellarchitected-performance-efficiency-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
This approach permits teams to focus on product development instead of resource provisioning and management. [wellarchitected-performance-efficiency-pillar.pdf, p. 9]

outcomes.question: What is mechanical sympathy?
outcomes.answer:
Mechanical sympathy involves understanding how cloud services are consumed and consistently using the technology approach that aligns best with your workload goals. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 45]
For instance, mechanical sympathy includes considering data access patterns when selecting database or storage approaches for a workload. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 45]

outcomes.question: Which database is suited to caching, session management and gaming leaderboards?
outcomes.answer:
In-memory databases can be used for application caching, session management, and gaming leaderboards. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 744]
AWS in-memory database services include Amazon ElastiCache and Amazon MemoryDB for Redis. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 744]

outcomes.question: How should failed Lambda transactions be retained and retried?
outcomes.answer:
A dead-letter queue mechanism should be used to retain, investigate, and retry failed transactions. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 60]
AWS Lambda enables sending failed transactions to an Amazon SQS dead-letter queue designated on a per-function basis. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 60]
Within AWS Lambda, retry during data record processing can be managed by configuring Maximum Retry Attempts, Maximum Record Age, and Destination on Failure. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 60]
Metadata for poison-pill messages can be removed from a batch and routed to an Amazon SQS dead-letter queue for further analysis. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 60]
Step Functions should be utilized when possible to reduce custom try/catch, back-off, and retry logic. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 60]

outcomes.question: What does Amazon API Gateway provide for serverless microservices?
outcomes.answer:
Amazon API Gateway hosts RESTful HTTP requests and responses to customers for RESTful microservices. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 15]
In a RESTful microservices scenario, Amazon API Gateway provides built-in authorization, throttling, security, fault tolerance, request and response mapping, and performance optimizations. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 15]
API Gateway handles tasks including traffic management, authorization and access control, monitoring, and API version management when accepting and processing up to hundreds of thousands of concurrent API calls. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 22]
The ability to make synchronous calls from API Gateway to AWS Lambda enables the creation of fully serverless applications. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 12]

outcomes.question: What can be considered to reduce the impact of Lambda cold starts?
outcomes.answer:
Provisioned concurrency initializes a requested number of execution environments so that they can respond immediately to function invocations. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 67]

outcomes.question: What options does AWS offer for service discovery of microservices?
outcomes.answer:
Amazon ECS provides integrated service discovery by managing a registry of service names using the Route 53 Auto Naming API. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 17]
Services managed by Kubernetes can use unified service discovery through AWS's contributions to the External DNS project. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 17]
AWS Cloud Map extends Auto Naming APIs by providing a service registry and an API-based discovery mechanism. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 17]
Third-party software such as HashiCorp Consul, etcd, or Netflix Eureka can also be used to implement service discovery. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 17]
Service meshes can handle tasks such as service discovery in microservices architectures. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 17]
AWS App Mesh can be utilized with service-oriented architectures to offer reliable discovery and access to services. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 65]

outcomes.question: What do twelve-factor processes say about state?
outcomes.answer:
Twelve-factor processes are stateless and share-nothing. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 14]
Any data that must persist has to be stored in a stateful backing service, which is typically a database. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 14]

outcomes.question: What does it mean to adopt a consumption model?
outcomes.answer:
Adopting a consumption model means paying only for the computing resources consumed, and increasing or decreasing usage based on business requirements. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 8]
For instance, development and test environments can be stopped when not in use to achieve potential cost savings of 75%. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 8]

outcomes.question: How does the cost optimization pillar suggest reducing cloud waste?
outcomes.answer:
Organizations should identify and recoup expenditure tied to cloud waste for resources that are deployed. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 28]
Cloud waste happens when incorrectly-sized resources are provisioned or when observed usage patterns deviate from expectations. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 28]
To reduce waste, organizations can follow AWS best practices or ask their account team and partner for assistance in optimizing and saving cloud costs. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 28]
Attributing resource costs to workloads, individual organizations, or product owners promotes efficient usage behavior and assists in reducing waste. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 37]

outcomes.question: Why does the choice of AWS Region matter for the carbon footprint of a workload?
outcomes.answer:
The selection of an AWS Region for a workload significantly influences its carbon footprint as well as other key performance indicators. [wellarchitected-sustainability-pillar.pdf, p. 23]
Deploying workloads in Regions near Amazon renewable energy projects or where the grid carbon intensity is low can reduce a workload's carbon footprint. [wellarchitected-sustainability-pillar.pdf, p. 23]

outcomes.question: What is the shared responsibility model for sustainability?
outcomes.answer:
Environmental sustainability is a shared responsibility between AWS and its customers. [wellarchitected-sustainability-pillar.pdf, p. 7]
AWS is responsible for sustainability of the cloud, which includes delivering efficient shared infrastructure, managing water stewardship, and sourcing renewable power. [wellarchitected-sustainability-pillar.pdf, p. 7]
Customers bear responsibility for sustainability in the cloud by optimizing workloads and resource utilization, as well as minimizing required workload resources. [wellarchitected-sustainability-pillar.pdf, p. 7]

outcomes.question: What does AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery do?
outcomes.answer:
AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery continuously replicates server-hosted applications and server-hosted databases from any source into AWS via block-level replication of the underlying server. [disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws.pdf, p. 26]
It allows an AWS Cloud Region to be used as a disaster recovery target for workloads hosted on-premises or on another cloud provider. [disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws.pdf, p. 26]
It can also support disaster recovery of AWS-hosted workloads if they consist solely of EC2-hosted applications and databases instead of RDS. [disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws.pdf, p. 26]
The service replicates data from a primary region to a recovery region using continuous data protection to target an RPO in seconds and an RTO in minutes. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 692]
Elastic Disaster Recovery manages and orchestrates the recovery of compute resources during a failover or drill. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 692]
